listen: Good morning. This is The Daily Brief for Wednesday, November 25. Here is what matters today. Our lead story is from the United States. Kilmar Abrego Garcia, a Salvadoran immigrant who became a symbol of President Trump's mass deportation campaign, left the country voluntarily on Tuesday. He went to Spain. His departure follows nearly two years of legal battles. The BBC says it ends the deportation fight. His deportation to El Salvador, and his return to the United States, became a flashpoint in the debate over the president's immigration agenda. Now the front page. In tech, Simon Willison has written up his keynote from the AI Engineer Code Summit. He argues there have been three significant inflection points in the abilities of language models and coding agents in the past twelve months. It is a useful read for anyone building tools with agents. In national security, the U.S. government is investigating Iranian ties to as many as fifty hacked commercial vessels. That is according to officials who spoke to NPR. And in China, authorities are investigating Politburo member and Shanghai party chief Chen Jining. He is the latest senior official targeted in President Xi Jinping's anti-corruption campaign. Now the sections. In tech and AI, a trending framework called Superpowers gives coding agents a set of composable skills. Another repository, CLI-Anything, aims to make existing software usable by agents. Anthropic also says it is committing a portion of its shares to a new Public Benefit Fund. In politics, The Lever asks economist Isabella Weber whether Democrats will take on corporate power over living costs. Drop Site News reports that displaced families in Gaza are lining their tents with sandbags because of frequent shootings. And Democrats are examining whether businesses tied to Donald Trump Junior's investment firm have benefited from government access. In world news, a New York jury found Huawei guilty of stealing American trade secrets, but acquitted it of racketeering. A spacecraft has returned to study an asteroid that was knocked off course four years ago. And a sports court gave the Africa Cup title back to Senegal. In sports, an MLB lockout is looming, and ESPN's experts suggest some last-minute trades. Infielder Ha-Seong Kim has reportedly agreed to a one-year, five million dollar deal with the Tigers. And Brock Purdy beat the league's most blitz-heavy defense in the 49ers' thirty-five to ten win over the Vikings. In Atlanta, a Fulton County judge ordered the county to hand over unredacted 2020 election records to the State Election Board, and the county has appealed. Georgia Tech named Timothy Lieuwen its permanent president. And Urbanize Atlanta looks at a Brookhaven firehouse dispute. In architecture, AtkinsRéalis and the University of Birmingham will partner on digital skills and AI. A new guide helps Horn of Africa cities prepare for El Niño rains. And a house in the Cauca River canyon in Colombia is designed around calm. In science, Webb has released a new image of the Cassiopeia A supernova remnant. NASA has locked in the design for a nuclear electric propulsion demonstration planned for 2028. And new research helps explain why Challenger Deep is the deepest spot in the ocean. That is the brief. Have a good day.

lead.title: Kilmar Abrego Garcia leaves U.S. voluntarily for Spain
lead.note: Kilmar Abrego Garcia, a Salvadoran immigrant who became a symbol of President Trump's mass deportation campaign, left the United States voluntarily on Tuesday. He traveled to Spain. NPR reports that his departure follows nearly two years of legal battles. The BBC says his exit ends the deportation fight. It also notes that his deportation to El Salvador, and his later return to the US, became a flashpoint in the debate over Trump's immigration agenda. That makes his departure the end of a case that lasted nearly two years. The case remains a reference point for the wider debate over immigration enforcement. The summaries do not say what terms led to his leaving or what comes next for him in Spain, so those details remain to be reported.
